store.handoff-records.no-payload-sort.why: Without this test, a payload-carrying ORDER BY would again spill megabytes to a temp file on a big board and stall next.

proves.claim: a claimed item whose gate is unknown on a missing main receipt is awaiting its gate.

store.submit-handoff-records.unknown-on-.why: Without this test, a lapsed claim on an unknown gate went to a fresh seat while the board still settles it.

proves.claim: a gate step pruned between its key and payload reads is skipped and handoffRecords returns the other records.

store.submit-handoff-records.pruned-step.why: Without this test, a pruned step crashed next with a TypeError on a missing row.

proves.claim: an unknown gate that settles red is no longer awaiting.

store.submit-handoff-records.unknown-set.why: Without this test, an unknown hold could outlive the red that settles it.

proves.claim: a gate created 3 h ago that offered its open shards 1 h ago is unsettled and awaiting its gate.

store.submit-handoff-records.hold-counts.why: Without this test, a gate that queued before its checks loses its hold with shards still open and next hands the lapsed claim to a fresh seat as you hold (#11921).

proves.claim: a gate offered 3 h ago with one shard still offered is unsettled and awaiting its gate.

store.submit-handoff-records.open-shard-.why: Without this test, a backlog longer than the fallback bound hands a gate's lapsed claim to a fresh seat while its shards still wait (#11923).

proves.claim: a gate offered 3 h ago with no open shard job is settled.

store.submit-handoff-records.no-open-sha.why: Without this test, an unbounded hold could keep the claim of a gate whose shards are gone or all done.

proves.claim: that late gate once it notes shards.settled red is settled and no longer holds the claim.

store.submit-handoff-records.late-gate-r.why: Without this test, counting the hold from the shard offer could keep a red gate's claim from returning as rework.

proves.claim: a seat silent for 3 minutes whose gate settled unknown keeps its claim with no release event.

store.stale-apply.silent-seat-keeps-unkn.why: Without this test, the seat-gone sweep could release a claim whose unknown gate still waits on main's receipt.

proves.claim: deliverHealthNotices given recentlyResolved and now logs but shouts no one for an added finding resolved under 30 minutes before, shouts after 30 minutes, and changes nothing below HEALTH_EPISODE_ENGINE.

store.logic-board-receipts.flap-within-3.why: Without it a finding that flaps would shout the coordinator every time it returns.

proves.claim: applyHealthFindings builds recentlyResolved from health-resolved events of the last 30 minutes by board clock, so a finding that resolves and returns 10 minutes later gets one Stuck shout.

store.io-board-health.flap-reads-recent-.why: Without it the flap rule would exist but the sentinel's real write path would never feed it.

proves.claim: appendFact records a note superseding the item's accept move when the caller recorded that accept.

store.board-fact.reviewer-corrects-accep.why: Without this test, a reviewer's untrue accept note could not be corrected on the record.

proves.claim: a seat that did not record the accept is refused FACT_JUDGEMENT and a supersedes naming nothing is refused NO_FACT.

store.board-fact.other-seat-cannot-corre.why: Without this test, any seat could rewrite another reviewer's verdict note.

proves.claim: buildLocalBoardState marks an accepted item whose only conflict with main is mechanical as fresh, and one with a real source conflict as stale naming the file.

store.io-board-state.mechanical-conflict.why: Without this test, the view's board state would call a mechanically resolvable conflict stale, or hide a real source conflict.

proves.claim: The state build reaches the mechanical-conflict reader through the board front door, which names only the file a mechanical merge cannot resolve.

store.io-board-state.production-wiring.why: Without this test, the state build could stop passing the reader and the view would show stale accepts the lander keeps.
